docs.title: 16S Amplicon Sequence Analysis for Predicting Colorectal Cancer
docs.text:
This website provides an example of an analysis report for 16S amplicon dataset with the goal to identify key biomarkers of gut microbiome for colorectal cancer prediction. The example comprises of a detailed report on gut microbiome abundance, host characteristics and their association with colorectal cancer.

The example presented utilizes a public dataset available online from (Zackular et al., 2014). The study investigated the potential of gut microbiome for predicting cases of colorectal cancer.

We used raw sequences (i.e., FASTQ files) from the study and applied our in-house processing pipeline to generate relative abundance dataset of microbiome.

docs.title: References
docs.text: 1. Zackular JP, Rogers MA, Ruffin MT 4th, Schloss PD. The human gut microbiome as a screening tool for colorectal cancer. Cancer Prev Res (Phila). 2014 Nov;7(11):1112-21. doi: 10.1158/1940-6207.CAPR-14-0129. Epub 2014 Aug 7. PMID: 25104642; PMCID: PMC4221363.

docs.title: Host characteristics
docs.text: This is the first exploration step which looks at host characteristics across cases under study (i.e., healthy, adenoma, carcinoma). We explore characteristics such as age, BMI and sex with the goal to identify any potential relationships with colon cancer.

docs.title: Microbial composition
docs.text:
This step visualize microbial compositions found in the sample across different cases. This visualization offers the first insights into types of microbiome present in the sample and whether there is any differences in the compositions.

The below figure shows composition of top 10 families in the sample across different groups.

docs.title: Alpha diversity
docs.text:
Alpha diversity measures provide insights into richness and evenness of species in a community. There are several measures available for computing alpha diversity. For example, Shannon, Chao1, Simpson, etc. Read more about alpha diversity here

We will use those measures to identify patterns of potential associations between alpha diversity and colorectal cancer.

The figure below shows four alpha diversity measuers (i.e., Cho1, Shannon, Simpson, InvSimpson) for normal, adenoma, and carcinoma cases of colorectal cancer.

Alpha diversity

Healthy individuals exhibit relatively higher alpha diversity compared to adenoma and carcinoma patients, with the difference being more pronounced between normal and adenoma groups.

docs.title: Microbial species at Phylum level
docs.text:
Abundant phylum

Bacteroidota, Firmicutes, and Verrucomicrobiota are the most abundance phylums present in the samples.

docs.title: Top-5 Families
docs.text:
The following figures show distribution of top-5 families across healthy, adenoma and carcinoma patients. The figures also show statistical significance of differences between groups in terms of relative abundance of five microbiome families (Wilcoxon rank test).

Ruminococcaceae

There is statistical significant differences between healthy and carcinoma patients in terms of relative abundance of Ruminococcaceae.
